paper.title: Combinatorial Multi-Armed Bandit with General Reward Functions

settings.name_in_paper: CMAB with general reward functions (semi-bandit feedback), unknown horizon
unmapped: General nonlinear reward R(x,S) whose expectation may depend on the full outcome distributions (not only means), bounded in [0,M] and monotone in outcomes
Base-arm outcomes mutually independent across arms, arbitrary distributions on [0,1]
Access to an alpha-approximation offline oracle taking finite-support distributions as input (not a linear optimization oracle strictly)
settings.definition_quote: We model a combinatorial multi-armed bandit (CMAB) problem as a tuple $(E, \calF, D, R)$, where $E = [m]$ is a set of $m$ (base) arms, $\calF \subseteq 2^{E}$ is a set of subsets of $E$, $D$ is a probability distribution over $[0, 1]^m$, and $R$ is a reward function defined on $[0, 1]^m \times \calF$.

settings.name_in_paper: CMAB with general reward functions (semi-bandit feedback), known horizon
unmapped: General nonlinear reward R(x,S) whose expectation may depend on the full outcome distributions, bounded in [0,M], monotone and Lipschitz in outcomes
Base-arm outcomes mutually independent across arms, arbitrary distributions on [0,1]
Access to an alpha-approximation offline oracle taking finite-support distributions as input
settings.definition_quote: Suppose the time horizon $T$ is known in advance. ... There exists $C>0$ such that for any $S \in \calF$ and any $x, x'\in [0, 1]^m$, we have $\left| R(x, S) - R(x', S) \right| \le C\|x_S - x_S'\|_1$

symbols.sum_bad: sum over base arms i in E_B (arms contained in at least one bad super arm)

conditions: alpha-approximation oracle available for finite-support distributions

source.label: thm:regret-bound-discrete
source.quote: A distribution-dependent upper bound on the $\alpha$-approximation regret of \texttt{SDCB} (Algorithm~\ref{alg:SDCB}) in $T$ rounds is $M^2 K \sum_{i\in E_\bad} \frac{2136}{\Delta_{i, \min}} \ln T + \left( \frac{\pi^2}{3} + 1 \right) \alpha Mm$

results.notes: Paper's K (max super-arm size) mapped to canonical m; paper's m (number of base arms) declared n_base. Regret defined via expected rewards r_D, i.e. pseudo alpha-regret. Compute polynomial per round excluding the oracle.

source.label: thm:bound-know-T
source.quote: Suppose the time horizon $T$ is known in advance. Then the $\alpha$-approximation regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:Lazy-SDCB} in $T$ rounds is at most $93 M \sqrt{ mK T \ln T} + 2CK\sqrt T + \left( \frac{\pi^2}{3} + 1 \right) \alpha Mm.$

results.notes: Paper's Lipschitz constant C mapped to L_lip. Total time O(T^{3/2}) excluding oracle.

source.label: thm:bound-not-know-T
source.quote: For any time horizon $T \ge 2$, the $\alpha$-approximation regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:Lazy-SDCB-unknown-T} in $T$ rounds is at most $318M \sqrt{mKT \ln T} + 7 CK \sqrt{T} + 10 \alpha Mm \ln T.$

results.notes: Lipschitz assumption recorded as a condition rather than setting feature.
